correctness.rationale: For exact masses the diagonal Gram entries equal γ and the off-diagonal modulus is |Z|/(2π); the cross term is 2 Re(conj(a)b Z)/(2π). Trimming surplus mass by nonatomicity lowers the integral strictly for nonzero coefficients if positive mass was removed. For the moment problem use independent upper level sets of cos(t−φ); cosine level sets have measure zero, giving uniqueness at fixed phase. Complementation negates Z. For l≤L/2 reduce by grid symmetry to 0≤φ≤L/2. The last cell is optimized at its right endpoint; in the second cell the two endpoint caps for φ≤l/2 have lengths l/2+φ and l/2−φ because their interior boundaries have equal cosine, and the first cell then takes [0,l]. For φ≥l/2 only the left cap survives and the first interval is centered. The sine boundary terms give 2sin(L+l/2)+2(sin l−sin L)cos φ in the first branch, and 2sin(l/2)[1+2cos((L+l)/2)cos(φ−L/2)] in the second. These increase strictly toward L/2 below half occupancy and are identically 1 at half occupancy. In the flat case each phase realizes the global modulus bound with that exact phase, so the masks are distinct up to null sets; their intervals vary continuously in measure. The explicit maximizer gives attainment; its Gram matrix is positive definite because a nonzero two-mode polynomial cannot vanish on positive measure. The eigenvector in the Finding has the correct phase. A separate cosine-sorting midpoint grid reproduced 427 bounded support tests (`python3 /workspace/frozen_review_replay.py 5`); this is numerical corroboration only. The frozen checker was read, not run.
